name: Jira MCP
tagline: Read, create, and update Jira issues from your AI agent.
shortDescription: The Atlassian Jira MCP server. Search issues, view details, create new tickets, transition status, add comments, and assign work. Full bidirectional sync with Jira Cloud.
longDescription:
## What it is

The official Atlassian MCP server for Jira Cloud. Exposes Jira's REST API as MCP tools: search (JQL), get/create/update/transition issues, add comments, manage sprints, list boards, and work with epics and stories.

## Why we recommend it

It comes from Atlassian, so the auth, rate limits, and edge cases are all handled correctly. The search-by-JQL feature is particularly useful — your agent can ask "what are the open P0 bugs assigned to me?" and get a structured answer. Comments and transitions round-trip without losing history.

## When to use it

- Engineering teams that use Jira and want Claude/Cursor to draft or summarize tickets
- Sprint planning: agent pulls current sprint state, suggests carryover
- Standup automation: agent pulls "yesterday/today/blockers" for each teammate
- Triage: agent classifies new issues by component, priority, and labels
installInstructions:
1. Get an Atlassian API token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
2. Set env vars: `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN`
3. `npx -y @atlassian/mcp-jira`

**Cloud only:** This server targets Jira Cloud. For Jira Server / Data Center, use a different integration.
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. Jira itself has a free tier (up to 10 users) and paid plans starting at $7.16/user/mo.
